stem: A transit agency records the delay (in minutes) of each of 60 commuter trains in one month. The histogram is strongly right-skewed: most delays are under 10 minutes, but a handful exceed two hours. An analyst wants one measure of center and one measure of spread that will not be distorted by those extreme delays. Which pair should the analyst report, and why?
criteria: A. Mean and IQR, because the mean gives the total delay spread evenly across all trains.
B. Median and range, because the range shows how bad the worst delays were.
C. (correct) Median and IQR, because both depend only on the ordered middle of the data and are not moved by a few very long delays.
D. Mean and standard deviation, because they take every train's delay into account and so reflect the whole month.

stem: A school counselor asks 80 teens how many text messages they sent yesterday. The distribution is strongly right-skewed with a five-number summary of: Min = 0, Q1 = 12, Median = 30, Q3 = 66, Max = 410. Which description of typical value and variation is most appropriate?
criteria: A. A median of 30 texts and a range of 410 texts, because the range shows the full spread of the data.
B. A median of 30 texts and an IQR of 36 texts, because the IQR is the distance from the median to Q3.
C. (correct) A median of 30 texts and an IQR of 54 texts, because neither is pulled by the few extremely high counts.
D. A mean and standard deviation, because they use all 80 reported values.

stem: A real estate agent reports that for homes sold in one neighborhood last year, the mean sale price was $410,000 and the median sale price was $325,000. A buyer asks for the single value that best represents a typical home price. Which response is best?
criteria: A. Report either one, because the mean and median always give the same typical value.
B. Report the mean of $410,000, because it accounts for every home's sale price.
C. (correct) Report the median of $325,000, because the mean is pulled above the typical home by a few very expensive sales.
D. Report the mean of $410,000, because the median ignores half of the data.

stem: Monthly rents for apartments listed in a city are strongly right-skewed because a few luxury units cost far more than the rest. A housing researcher wants to describe the typical rent and how much rents vary. Which pair of statistics is most appropriate?
criteria: A. Median and range, since the range includes all of the listings.
B. Mean and IQR, since the IQR is the only resistant spread measure.
C. Mean and standard deviation, since they are the most commonly used.
D. (correct) Median and IQR, since luxury listings barely affect either one.

stem: A biologist measures the wingspan of 120 randomly captured adults of one bird species. A histogram is symmetric and mound-shaped with no outliers. Which pair of statistics is most appropriate to describe the center and spread?
criteria: A. (correct) Mean and SD, since a symmetric distribution without outliers does not distort them.
B. Mean and range, since the range reports the distance between the two extreme wingspans.
C. Median and IQR, since they should always be used no matter what shape the data have.
D. Median and range, since the range is the easiest spread measure to compute.

stem: The waiting times (in minutes) of 150 patients at an urgent care clinic are strongly right-skewed with five-number summary: Min = 2, Q1 = 10, Median = 14, Q3 = 19, Max = 90. Which pair of values best describes the center and spread of the waiting times?
criteria: A. (correct) Median = 14 minutes and IQR = 9 minutes, since neither is affected much by the 90-minute wait.
B. Median = 14 minutes and range = 88 minutes, since the range shows the full spread.
C. Median = 14 minutes and spread = 17 minutes, since that is the distance from the minimum to Q3.
D. Median = 14 minutes and spread = 5 minutes, since that is the distance from the median to Q3.

stem: A quiz has these scores: 5, 6, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 52. If the largest score were changed from 52 to 520, which summary would stay exactly the same?
criteria: A. The standard deviation, which stays near 16.
B. The range, which stays at 47.
C. The mean, which stays at 12.75.
D. (correct) The median, which stays at 7.5.

stem: A technician records the times (in seconds) for 8 lab trials: 12, 14, 15, 15, 16, 18, 19, 30. The 30 was later found to be a typing error for 300. Which statistic would be least affected by this error?
criteria: A. The range, because it only involves the two ends of the data.
B. The standard deviation, because it measures typical deviation from the mean.
C. The mean, because averaging dilutes one value among eight.
D. (correct) The IQR, which is 4 seconds with either value.

stem: A teacher's quiz scores are 62, 68, 71, 74, 75, 77, 79 (mean about 72.3, median 74). A late student then turns in a quiz with a score of 3. Which statement about the effect of the new score is correct?
criteria: A. Neither the mean nor the median changed, since only one score was added.
B. The mean and median both fell by about 8.7 points, since both measure center.
C. The median fell by about 8.7 points while the mean fell only 1.5, since the median is the middle value.
D. (correct) The mean fell by about 8.7 points to 63.6, while the median fell by only 1.5 points to 72.5.

stem: For the lengths of 200 randomly selected leaves, a botanist reports a mean of 52.4 mm, a median of 52.1 mm, and a standard deviation of 6.0 mm. Which conclusion about the shape is most reasonable?
criteria: A. The distribution is right-skewed, since the mean is larger than the median.
B. The distribution is left-skewed, since the median is close to the mean rather than far above it.
C. Nothing can be said about shape, since the mean and median describe only center.
D. (correct) The distribution is roughly symmetric, since the mean and median are nearly equal compared to the spread.

stem: The commute times of 300 workers have a mean of 38 minutes and a median of 29 minutes. Which description of the distribution is most consistent with these values?
criteria: A. Left-skewed, because most workers have commutes shorter than the mean.
B. Left-skewed, because the mean is greater than the median.
C. Symmetric, because the mean and median are both measures of center.
D. (correct) Right-skewed, because a few long commutes pull the mean above the median.

stem: The ages at which employees at a large company retired form a left-skewed distribution, with a few people retiring in their early forties and most retiring in their sixties. Which statement is most likely true?
criteria: A. The mean and median retirement ages are exactly equal.
B. The mean retirement age is greater than the median retirement age.
C. (correct) The mean retirement age is less than the median retirement age.
D. The median is pulled further toward the early retirees than the mean is.

stem: A gardener wants to compare two fertilizers using 24 tomato plants in a garden where half the plants are in full sun and half are in shade, and sunlight strongly affects growth. Which plan uses blocking?
criteria: A. Apply fertilizer A to all sun plants and fertilizer B to all shade plants.
B. (correct) Separate the plants into sun and shade groups, then randomly assign fertilizers within each group.
C. Flip a coin for each plant to choose its fertilizer, ignoring sunlight.
D. Use only the sun plants and randomly assign the two fertilizers.

stem: Researchers compare two study methods using students whose prior GPAs vary widely, and they place students into 'high GPA' and 'low GPA' blocks before randomly assigning methods within each block. What is the main purpose of blocking here?
criteria: A. (correct) To remove variation due to prior GPA so method differences are easier to detect.
B. To remove the need for random assignment of methods to students.
C. To make sure the sample is representative of every student in the school.
D. To make sure neither the students nor the graders know which method was used.

stem: To compare two exercise programs, a researcher separates 60 volunteers into a male group and a female group, then within each group uses a random number generator to assign half to Program 1 and half to Program 2. Which description is most accurate?
criteria: A. (correct) A randomized block experiment, with sex as the blocking variable.
B. A completely randomized design, since random assignment was used.
C. A stratified random sample, since subjects were grouped by sex.
D. An observational study, since sex cannot be assigned.

stem: Students are randomly assigned to use a tutoring app or a traditional workbook. The final tests are scored by a teacher who is not told which students used which method. What is the main benefit of having the scorer blinded?
criteria: A. (correct) It prevents the scorer's expectations about the app from influencing the scores.
B. It removes confounding variables such as prior ability.
C. It prevents the students' expectations from affecting their performance.
D. It makes the sample representative of all students.

stem: In a study of a headache remedy, a placebo group's pain score improved by an average of 4.1 points, while a no-treatment group's pain score improved by an average of 1.3 points. Using the definition of placebo effect as the difference between the average placebo response and the average no-treatment response, what is the placebo effect?
criteria: A. 5.4 points
B. 4.1 points
C. (correct) 2.8 points
D. 0 points, because a placebo contains no active ingredient.

stem: Which setup for a trial of a new cholesterol drug is double-blind?
criteria: A. (correct) Identical-looking capsules coded by pharmacy; neither patients nor the clinicians recording outcomes know assignments.
B. All patients receive the drug and both patients and clinicians know it.
C. Patients are unaware of what they receive, but the clinician recording outcomes knows each assignment.
D. Patients choose between the drug and a placebo, but clinicians do not know who chose which.

stem: For a marketing email, 45% of recipients open the message. Among those who open it, 20% click the link. What is the probability that a randomly selected recipient both opens the email and clicks the link?
criteria: B. (correct) 0.09

stem: A student passes the first exam of a course with probability 0.80. If the student passes the first exam, the probability of passing the second exam is 0.75. What is the probability that the student passes both exams?
criteria: D. (correct) 0.60

stem: In a three-step security check, 50% of travelers pass step 1. Of those, 40% pass step 2. Of those who pass steps 1 and 2, 90% pass step 3. What proportion of all travelers pass all three steps?
criteria: B. (correct) 0.18

stem: Which of the following random variables has a binomial distribution?
criteria: A. (correct) The number of heads in 15 flips of a fair coin.
B. The number of flips needed until the first head appears.
C. The sum of the faces in 10 rolls of a fair die.
D. The number of hearts in a 5-card hand dealt without replacement from a standard deck.

stem: A quality inspector randomly selects 12 bulbs from a very large shipment, where each bulb is independently defective with probability 0.03. Let X be the number of defective bulbs. Which statement correctly justifies that X is binomial?
criteria: A. X is binomial because the defect probability is small.
B. X is binomial because it takes whole-number values.
C. (correct) There are a fixed 12 trials, each with two outcomes, independent, with constant P(defective) = 0.03.
D. X is binomial because the sample is large enough for X to be approximately normal.

stem: A teacher randomly picks 6 students one at a time, without replacement, from a class of 20 students (10 girls and 10 boys). Let X be the number of girls selected. Why is X not binomial?
criteria: A. The probability of selecting a girl, 0.5, is too large for a binomial model.
B. (correct) Picking without replacement from a small class makes trials dependent, so P(girl) shifts.
C. The number of picks is not fixed in advance by the teacher.
D. Each pick has more than two possible outcomes for the student chosen.

stem: A 90% confidence interval for a population proportion, based on a random sample of 400 voters, has a margin of error of 0.04. If the pollsters instead sampled 1600 voters, with the same confidence level and about the same sample proportion, what would the margin of error be approximately?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.02

stem: A poll of 500 randomly chosen adults gives a 90% confidence interval for a population proportion. If the pollster keeps the same data but reports a 99% confidence interval, what happens to the margin of error?
criteria: A. (correct) It gets larger, because the critical value z* increases from about 1.645 to about 2.576.
B. It stays the same, because the standard error depends only on n and p̂.
C. It gets smaller, because greater confidence means a more precise estimate.
D. It gets larger, because 99% confidence needs a larger sample.

stem: A researcher wants a 95% confidence interval for a population proportion with a margin of error no larger than 0.03, and has no prior estimate of the proportion. Using z* = 1.96 and the most conservative p̂ = 0.5, what is the minimum sample size?
criteria: C. (correct) 1068

stem: A significance test of H0: p = 0.5 at α = 0.05 has a 0.32 probability of failing to reject H0 when the true proportion is 0.6. What is the power of the test against p = 0.6?
criteria: C. (correct) 0.68

stem: A researcher tests H0: p = 0.50 against Ha: p > 0.50 with n = 100 and α = 0.05. Which change would increase the power of the test against the true value p = 0.60?
criteria: A. Decreasing the sample size to 25.
B. (correct) Increasing the sample size to 400.
C. Testing against a true value closer to H0, such as 0.52.
D. Decreasing α to 0.01.

stem: A pharmaceutical company tests H0: the new drug has no effect on blood pressure, against Ha: the drug lowers blood pressure. Which statement correctly describes the power of this test?
criteria: A. The probability of failing to reject H0 when the drug does lower blood pressure.
B. The probability that the drug lowers blood pressure given that H0 was rejected.
C. The probability of rejecting H0 when the drug has no effect.
D. (correct) The probability of rejecting H0 when the drug really does lower blood pressure by a specific amount.

stem: A plant has three machines. Machine A makes 50% of items with a 2% defect rate; Machine B makes 30% with a 3% defect rate; Machine C makes 20% with a 5% defect rate. A randomly selected item is defective. What is the probability it came from Machine B?
criteria: A. About 0.030
B. About 0.300
C. About 0.009
D. (correct) About 0.310

stem: A school tracks whether students studied and whether they passed. Which expression correctly gives P(studied | passed)?
criteria: A. P(studied)P(passed)
B. P(passed | studied)P(passed)
C. P(studied) / P(passed | studied)
D. (correct) P(passed | studied)P(studied) / P(passed)

stem: A school surveyed 400 commuters, grouped by mode, and recorded who arrived late this month: Bus 160 (24 late), Bike 100 (15 late), Car 140 (11 late). Among all students who arrived late, what is the probability a randomly chosen late arrival is a bike rider?
criteria: D. (correct) 0.30

stem: A raffle ticket pays $10 with probability 0.5, $20 with probability 0.3, and $30 with probability 0.2. What is the expected payout of a ticket?
criteria: D. (correct) $17

stem: In a carnival game, a player wins $5 with probability 0.1, wins $1 with probability 0.3, and loses $2 with probability 0.6. What is the expected net winnings per play?
criteria: C. (correct) -$0.40

stem: A random variable X takes values 0, 2, and 5 with P(X = 0) = 0.25 and P(X = 2) = 0.35. What is E(X)?
criteria: D. (correct) 2.7

stem: Priya scored 83 on a chemistry exam whose scores have mean 74 and standard deviation 6. Marcus scored 68 on a history exam whose scores have mean 61 and standard deviation 4. Which student performed better relative to the other students who took the same exam?
criteria: A. (correct) Marcus, because his z-score of 1.75 is higher than Priya's z-score of 1.5.
B. Priya, because her score is about 1.12 times her exam's mean, compared with about 1.11 times for Marcus.
C. Priya, because she is 9 points above her mean while Marcus is only 7 points above his.
D. Priya, because her raw score of 83 is higher than Marcus's raw score of 68.

stem: Lena earns $52,000 at a firm where salaries have mean $45,000 and standard deviation $4,000. Omar earns $61,000 at a different firm where salaries have mean $50,000 and standard deviation $7,000. Relative to the pay at their own firms, who is paid better?
criteria: A. Omar, because his salary is 22% above his firm's mean while Lena's is only 16% above hers.
B. Omar, because he earns $11,000 above his firm's mean while Lena earns only $7,000 above hers.
C. Omar, because $61,000 is a larger salary than $52,000.
D. (correct) Lena, because her z-score of 1.75 exceeds Omar's z-score of about 1.57.

stem: Tom scored 35 on a placement test with mean 50 and standard deviation 10. Sue scored 58 on a different placement test with mean 50 and standard deviation 4. Whose result is farther from the typical score on her or his own test, measured in standard deviations?
criteria: A. (correct) Sue's, because her z-score of 2.0 is larger in absolute value than Tom's z-score of -1.5.
B. Tom's, because 35 is lower than 58.
C. Tom's, because he is 15 points from his mean while Sue is only 8 points from hers.
D. Neither, because Tom's negative z-score of -1.5 shows he performed worse than Sue and the two cannot be compared.

stem: Waiting times at a walk-in clinic are strongly right-skewed with standard deviation 12 minutes. A researcher repeatedly takes simple random samples of patients and computes the sample mean waiting time. Compare the sampling distribution of the sample mean for n = 20 patients with that for n = 80 patients.
criteria: A. The shape is closer to normal for n = 80, and the standard error is cut to one-fourth, from about 2.7 to about 0.7 minutes.
B. The shape is closer to normal for n = 80, but the standard error stays at 12 minutes for both sample sizes.
C. The shape is still right-skewed like the population for both sizes, and the standard error is cut in half from about 2.7 to about 1.3 minutes.
D. (correct) The shape is closer to normal for n = 80, and the standard error is cut in half, from about 2.7 to about 1.3 minutes.

stem: A hospital studies lengths of stay, which are right-skewed with standard deviation 6 days. The mean stay in a random sample of 36 patients is compared with the mean stay in a random sample of 144 patients. How do the standard errors of the two sample means compare?
criteria: A. The two samples have the same standard error of 6 days, since both come from the same population.
B. The sample of 144 has one-fourth the standard error of the sample of 36: 0.25 days versus 1.0 days.
C. The sample of 144 has twice the standard error of the sample of 36, because more patients add more variation.
D. (correct) The sample of 144 has half the standard error of the sample of 36: 0.5 days versus 1.0 days.

stem: Daily rainfall in a region is strongly right-skewed, with mean 3 mm and standard deviation 4 mm. Random samples of 64 days are taken and the sample mean rainfall is computed for each. Which description of the sampling distribution of the sample mean is best?
criteria: A. (correct) Approximately normal, with mean 3 mm and standard error 0.5 mm.
B. Right-skewed like the population, with mean 3 mm and standard error 0.5 mm.
C. Approximately normal, with mean 0.375 mm and standard error 0.5 mm.
D. Approximately normal, with mean 3 mm and standard error 4 mm.

stem: The heights of seedlings in a greenhouse have mean 35 cm and standard deviation 4 cm. What is the z-score of a seedling that is 29 cm tall?
criteria: C. (correct) -1.5

stem: Package delivery times for a courier have mean 64 minutes and standard deviation 5 minutes. A particular delivery took 72 minutes. What is its z-score?
criteria: A. (correct) 1.6

stem: The time for a school's students to finish a puzzle has mean 12.5 minutes and standard deviation 2.5 minutes. A student finishes in 10 minutes. Find the z-score for this student.
criteria: B. (correct) -1.0

stem: Six commute times (in minutes), listed in order, are 3, 5, 7, 8, 12, 15. What is the median commute time?
criteria: A. (correct) 7.5

stem: A researcher has 30 test scores arranged from smallest to largest. Which description locates the median of these scores?
criteria: A. The 15th ordered score alone.
B. (correct) The mean of the 15th and 16th ordered scores.
C. The mean of the 1st and 30th ordered scores.
D. The 16th ordered score alone, since 30/2 + 1 = 16.

stem: The monthly rainfall totals (mm) for a city, sorted from least to greatest, are 4, 6, 6, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 18, 21, 25, 40. What is the median?
criteria: C. (correct) 12.5

stem: A city council wants a simple random sample of 40 residents from a registry listing 2,000 residents. Which procedure best accomplishes this?
criteria: A. Interview the first 40 people who walk into city hall on Monday morning.
B. Take the first 40 residents on the registry, which is sorted by last name.
C. (correct) Number the residents 1 to 2,000 and use a random number generator to draw 40 different numbers.
D. Mail a survey to all residents and use the first 40 that are returned.

stem: A gym has 250 members and wants feedback from a simple random sample of 25 of them. Which plan is best?
criteria: A. Post a sign inviting members to take a survey and use the first 25 who respond.
B. Ask the 25 members who are nearest the front desk at noon on Tuesday.
C. Survey the 25 members who visit the gym most often.
D. (correct) Give each member an ID from 1 to 250 and have software pick 25 different IDs at random.

stem: A principal wants a simple random sample of 50 seniors from the 400 students in the senior class. Which method should she use?
criteria: A. Select the 50 seniors who have the highest grade point averages.
B. (correct) Number the seniors 1 to 400 and use a random number generator for 50 distinct numbers.
C. Announce a pizza party and take the first 50 seniors who sign up for it.
D. Ask each of the 10 homeroom teachers to hand-pick the 5 students they prefer.

stem: Public health data show that in months when ice cream sales are higher, more drownings occur. Which of the following is a plausible confounding variable for this association?
criteria: A. The year in which the data were recorded, with no link to either quantity
B. The correlation between the monthly ice cream sales and drownings
C. (correct) Hot weather, which draws more people to swim and also increases ice cream purchases
D. The number of drownings reported in each month

stem: A school district finds that students who take piano lessons score higher on math tests than students who do not. Which is a plausible confounding variable?
criteria: A. The p-value from comparing the math scores of the two groups
B. (correct) Family income, which could affect both lesson enrollment and math scores
C. The total number of students included in the district study
D. The average math score earned by the group of students taking lessons

stem: An observational study finds that adults who wear fitness trackers have lower body mass index (BMI), on average, than adults who do not. Which is a plausible confounding variable?
criteria: A. (correct) Health consciousness, causing people to wear trackers and keep a lower BMI
B. The test statistic used to compare BMI between the two groups
C. The BMI values that were measured for the adults in the study
D. The number of adults who were included in the study sample group

stem: A city health department inspects every one of the 312 restaurants in the city. Which term best describes the way these data were collected?
criteria: A. (correct) A census, because every restaurant in the population was included
B. A cluster sample, because restaurants are grouped by neighborhood
C. A systematic sample, because inspectors go through restaurants in street-address order
D. A convenience sample, because easy-to-reach restaurants were inspected

stem: A company with 1,200 employees emails its satisfaction survey to every employee. What is the best name for this data collection method?
criteria: A. (correct) A census of the company's employees
B. A stratified random sample by department
C. A voluntary response sample
D. A simple random sample of 1,200 employees

stem: A zoo veterinarian weighs all 15 giraffes at the zoo to describe the herd. What is this called?
criteria: A. A random sample of giraffes
B. (correct) A census of the herd
C. An experiment
D. A convenience sample

stem: At a school carnival, a prize wheel pays $20 with probability 0.15, $5 with probability 0.30, and $0 otherwise. What are a player's expected winnings per spin?
criteria: D. (correct) $4.50

stem: The number of pets X owned by a randomly chosen student has this distribution: P(X = 0) = 0.1, P(X = 1) = 0.4, P(X = 2) = 0.3, P(X = 3) = 0.2. What is the expected value of X?
criteria: C. (correct) 1.6

stem: An insurance company sells a policy for $60. With probability 0.02 it pays a claim of $2,000, and otherwise it pays nothing. What is the company's expected profit per policy, after the claim cost but including the $60 premium?
criteria: A. (correct) $20

stem: A population has standard deviation 14. Researchers take one random sample of 49 observations and another of 196 observations and compute each sample mean. Which sample mean has the smaller standard error, and what are the two standard errors?
criteria: A. (correct) The sample of 196, with standard errors of 2.0 for n = 49 and 1.0 for n = 196
B. The sample of 49, with standard errors of 1.0 for n = 49 and 2.0 for n = 196
C. The sample of 196, with standard errors of 0.29 for n = 49 and 0.07 for n = 196
D. Neither; both have a standard error of 14 because they come from the same population

stem: A random sample of n = 30 is used to estimate a population mean. By what sample size would the standard error of the sample mean be exactly half as large?
criteria: B. (correct) n = 120

stem: Commute times in a district have standard deviation 10 minutes. A simple random sample of 25 students is taken. What is the standard error of the sample mean commute time?
criteria: A. 50 minutes
B. 0.4 minutes
C. 10 minutes
D. (correct) 2.0 minutes

stem: A test of whether a tutoring program raises mean scores gives a p-value of 0.032. The significance level chosen before the study was alpha = 0.01. What is the appropriate decision?
criteria: A. (correct) Fail to reject H0, because 0.032 is greater than 0.01
B. Fail to reject H0 and conclude the tutoring program has no effect
C. Reject H0, because the p-value is greater than alpha, showing a significant result
D. Reject H0, because 0.032 is below the conventional 0.05 cutoff

stem: A company tests H0: mu = 10 hours against Ha: mu is not 10 hours for the mean battery life of a new phone. The test gives a p-value of 0.003, and alpha = 0.05. Which conclusion is correct?
criteria: A. (correct) Reject H0; there is convincing evidence the mean battery life differs from 10 hours.
B. Reject H0, because there is only a 0.3% chance that H0 is true
C. Fail to reject H0, because the p-value of 0.003 is smaller than alpha
D. Reject H0, which proves the true mean is not exactly 10 hours

stem: A one-sample test of a population mean results in a p-value of 0.07. The researcher specified alpha = 0.10 before collecting data. What decision should be made?
criteria: A. Fail to reject H0, because 0.07 is greater than the usual 0.05 cutoff
B. Reject H0 and conclude the probability H0 is true is 7%
C. Make no decision until the test statistic is converted to a z-score
D. (correct) Reject H0, because 0.07 is less than 0.10

stem: In a chi-square test of independence, one cell of the table has row total 60, column total 90, and the table total is 300. What is the expected count for that cell?
criteria: A. (correct) 18

stem:
A random sample of students was classified by class year and favorite study method:
Study method: Flash cards | Notes | Videos | Row total
Freshman: 30 | 45 | 25 | 100
Sophomore: 40 | 55 | 45 | 140
Column total: 70 | 100 | 70 | table total 240
If class year and study method are independent, what is the expected count for freshmen who prefer videos?
criteria: A. (correct) About 29.2
C. About 33.3

stem: A chi-square test of independence for 500 survey respondents focuses on one cell. The observed count in that cell is 48, its row total is 200, its column total is 150, and the table total is 500. What is the expected count for this cell?
criteria: D. (correct) 60

stem: In a clinical trial, researchers test H0: the new drug has no effect on blood pressure. They conclude the drug lowers blood pressure, but in fact the drug has no effect. Which type of error did they make?
criteria: A. Type II error, because the drug was wrongly judged effective
B. (correct) Type I error, because a true null hypothesis was rejected
C. Sampling bias, because the researchers used a sample
D. No error, because the conclusion followed from the sample results

stem: A quality inspector tests H0: mu = 500 g for the mean fill of cereal boxes. The machine has actually drifted so that the true mean is not 500 g, but the inspector fails to reject H0. What type of error is this?
criteria: A. Type I error, because the machine was not repaired
B. Type I error, because the inspector reached the wrong conclusion
C. (correct) Type II error, because a false null hypothesis was not rejected
D. No error, because failing to reject H0 is the safe decision

stem: A researcher tests H0 at significance level alpha = 0.05 and obtains a p-value of 0.03, so H0 is rejected. If H0 is actually true, what is the probability that this testing procedure produces a Type I error?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.05, which is the significance level alpha
B. 0.97, which is 1 - the p-value
C. 0.03, which is the observed p-value
D. 0.95, which is 1 - alpha

stem: A university health center reports that students who sleep at least 8 hours per night have a higher mean GPA than students who sleep less. The report is based on an email survey in which 320 students chose to respond and reported their own sleep and GPA. Which conclusion is appropriately supported by this study design?
criteria: A. Since sleep was not randomly assigned, the survey shows no relationship between sleep and GPA among respondents.
B. Sleeping at least 8 hours per night causes students to earn higher GPAs.
C. Because 320 respondents is a large sample, the data show that more sleep causes a higher GPA.
D. (correct) Sleep duration and GPA are associated among these respondents, but a cause-and-effect conclusion is not supported because sleep was not randomly assigned.

stem: A clinic recruits 90 volunteers with mild insomnia and uses a random number generator to assign 45 to drink a new herbal tea nightly and 45 to drink a placebo tea. After four weeks, the tea group fell asleep an average of 12 minutes faster, and a significance test shows this difference is very unlikely to be due to chance alone. Which conclusion is best supported?
criteria: A. (correct) The tea very likely caused faster sleep onset among these volunteers, because treatments were randomly assigned and the difference is unlikely to be due to chance.
B. The tea would cause faster sleep onset for all adults with insomnia, because random assignment makes the volunteers representative of them.
C. Because the participants were volunteers, no cause-and-effect conclusion is possible for anyone in the study.
D. Because only 90 people took part, no cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn from this study.

stem: Researchers select a simple random sample of 800 adults from a county and record how many cups of coffee each drinks per day and whether each has been diagnosed with heart disease. Adults who drink 3 or more cups a day have a lower rate of diagnosed heart disease than those who drink fewer. Which conclusion is appropriate?
criteria: A. The association cannot be generalized to the county's adults, because coffee drinking was not randomly assigned.
B. Drinking 3 or more cups of coffee a day lowers the risk of heart disease, because the sample was randomly selected.
C. Random selection ensures that age, diet, and other variables are balanced between heavy and light coffee drinkers, so differences are due to coffee.
D. (correct) There is an association in the county's adults that can be generalized because of the random sample, but causation cannot be concluded because coffee drinking was not assigned.

stem: A hospital analyst takes a random sample of n = 60 patients from a very large patient population in which the true readmission rate is p = 0.05. The analyst wants to use a normal approximation for the sampling distribution of the sample proportion who are readmitted. Why is this approximation not appropriate?
criteria: A. p = 0.05 is below 0.5, so the sampling distribution of p-hat can only be approximately normal when p is at least 0.5.
B. The sample size n = 60 is under 100, and a normal approximation needs at least 100 observations whatever the value of p.
C. (correct) np = 60(0.05) = 3, which is less than 10, so the large-counts condition fails and the sampling distribution of p-hat is skewed right.
D. The true rate p is known, so the sampling distribution of p-hat has no standard deviation to approximate with a normal model.

stem: A botanist plants a random sample of n = 50 seeds from a very large seed lot in which the true germination rate is p = 0.96. Which statement correctly evaluates using a normal approximation for the sampling distribution of the sample proportion that germinate?
criteria: A. (correct) The approximation is not appropriate, since n(1 − p) = 50(0.04) = 2 is less than 10, which leaves the distribution of p-hat skewed left.
B. The approximation is appropriate, because n = 50 is at least 30, which is the sample-size requirement for normality.
C. The approximation is inappropriate because p = 0.96 is greater than 0.5, and normal approximations require p ≤ 0.5.
D. The approximation is appropriate, because np = 50(0.96) = 48 is at least 10.

stem: A human resources office has 600 employees. It plans to take a simple random sample of n = 80 employees and use a normal model for the sampling distribution of the proportion who support a new schedule, where the true proportion is p = 0.40. Which statement identifies the problem with this plan?
criteria: A. There is no problem: np = 32 and n(1 − p) = 48 are both at least 10, so every condition for a normal model is met.
B. Because p = 0.40 is not close to 0.50, the large-counts condition fails and a normal model cannot be used.
C. Since 80 is much smaller than 600, the sample is too small relative to the population for the sampling distribution to be normal.
D. (correct) The sample of 80 is more than 10% of the 600 employees (10% of 600 is 60), so the independence (10%) condition is not met.

stem: A teacher has 15 quiz scores with a mean of 72. While rechecking, she corrects one score from 64 to 79 and recomputes the mean. How does the mean change?
criteria: A. (correct) It increases by 1.0, because the total of the scores rises by 15 and there are 15 scores.
B. It increases by about 1.07, because the total rises by 15 and is divided by 14.
C. It does not change, because changing one score does not affect the median.
D. It increases by 15.

stem: A data set of 20 commute times (in minutes) has a mean of 55. One entry of 90 minutes is found to be a typing error and is corrected to 50 minutes. What happens to the mean?
criteria: A. It decreases by about 2.1, because the total drops by 40 and is divided by 19.
B. It decreases by 40.
C. It increases by 2, because the size of the change, 40, is divided by 20 values.
D. (correct) It decreases by 2, because the total drops by 40 minutes and is shared among 20 values.

stem: A set of 8 measurements has a mean of 25. A lab technician replaces one measurement of 10 with a new measurement of 34. How does the mean change?
criteria: A. (correct) It increases by 3, because the total rises by 24 and there are 8 measurements.
B. It increases by 24.
C. It increases by 2.4, because the 24-point change is spread over 10 measurements.
D. It increases by 4.5, because the new mean is the average of the old mean, 25, and the new value, 34.

stem: A boxplot of the number of minutes students spent on homework has Q1 = 42 and Q3 = 58. Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, what is the upper fence for possible outliers?
criteria: C. (correct) 82

stem: For a set of delivery times (in minutes), Q1 = 120 and Q3 = 150. Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, what is the lower fence for possible outliers?
criteria: D. (correct) 75

stem: The daily change in temperature (in °F) for a city has Q1 = 20 and Q3 = 44. Using the 1.5 × IQR rule, which of the following values would be identified as a possible outlier?
criteria: C. (correct) 84

stem: A county library system has members who mostly use urban branches, a smaller group who use suburban branches, and only about 8% who use rural branches. The system plans a satisfaction survey of 500 members. Why might a stratified random sample be better than a simple random sample here?
criteria: A. (correct) It guarantees that the small rural group is included in a planned amount, which a simple random sample could under-represent by chance.
B. It is the only method in which every library member has the same chance of being selected.
C. It lets surveyors hand-pick willing members within each branch type, which gives more complete responses.
D. It removes sampling variability, so the sample percentages will equal the population percentages exactly.

stem: A factory has 300 day-shift, 150 evening-shift, and 50 night-shift workers. A manager wants to compare job satisfaction across the three shifts using a sample of 60 workers. Why might stratified sampling be preferable to a simple random sample of 60?
criteria: A. It removes the need to randomize, because the shifts are already natural groups of workers.
B. It selects entire shifts at random and surveys everyone in them, which saves time and travel.
C. It guarantees that no selected worker will refuse to answer, so the results are free of nonresponse bias.
D. (correct) Randomly sampling within each shift guarantees that the small night shift appears in the sample, so shifts can be compared.

stem: A pollster will survey 600 voters in a state whose regions differ sharply in their support for a ballot measure, while voters within a region tend to share similar views. Why might sampling randomly within each region give a more precise estimate than a simple random sample of 600?
criteria: A. It ensures that every possible group of 600 voters has the same chance of being selected, as in a simple random sample.
B. The pollster can choose the most typical voters in each region, which makes the sample more precise.
C. It guarantees that the sample proportion for the state equals the true statewide proportion.
D. (correct) Voters within each region are alike, so sampling within regions reduces variability in the statewide estimate compared with a simple random sample of 600.

stem: A track coach randomly assigns 24 runners to either a new stretching routine or the usual warm-up, then compares their 5K times at the end of the season. What does random assignment help with most?
criteria: A. Making sure the 24 runners are representative of all runners in the league.
B. Guaranteeing that the two groups have exactly the same mean 5K time before the routines begin.
C. Keeping the runners from knowing which routine they received.
D. (correct) Making the two groups similar in traits like fitness level, so a time difference can reasonably be attributed to the routine.

stem: A pharmacy randomly assigns 60 volunteers with a mild rash to use either a new cream or the standard cream for two weeks and then rates how much each rash improved. What does random assignment help with most?
criteria: A. Ensuring that each cream group contains exactly the same number of men as women.
B. (correct) Tending to balance known and unknown variables, like age and skin sensitivity, across the cream groups.
C. Removing measurement error from the rash-improvement ratings.
D. Making sure the volunteers represent all adults who develop rashes.

stem: A software company randomly shows each visitor to its site either layout A or layout B and compares the percent of visitors who sign up for a trial. What does random assignment help with most?
criteria: A. Making sure the visitors tested match the company's overall customer base.
B. (correct) Making visitors who see layout A comparable to those who see B, so a difference in sign-up rates can be attributed to the layout.
C. Ensuring the visitors cannot tell that two layouts are being compared, making the study blind.
D. Guaranteeing that both layout groups contain exactly the same number of returning customers.

stem: Of 60 employees at a company, 15 carpool to work and 20 arrive early. Six employees both carpool and arrive early. What is P(arrives early | carpools)?
criteria: A. (correct) 6/15 = 0.40

stem: In a school of 120 students, 48 are in band and 30 are in orchestra. Eighteen students are in both. What is P(in orchestra | in band)?

A store surveyed 200 customers and recorded age group and whether they bought online. The results are below.
Under 30, bought online: 50
Under 30, did not buy online: 30
30 or older, bought online: 40
30 or older, did not buy online: 80
What is P(under 30 | bought online)?
The probability that a randomly selected bulb from a production line is defective is 0.08. What is the probability that the bulb is not defective?
criteria: B. (correct) 0.92

stem: The probability that a certain flight arrives on time is 0.82. What is the probability that the flight does not arrive on time?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.18

stem: A forecaster says there is a 40% chance of snow tomorrow. What is the probability that it does not snow?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.60

stem: At a school, the probability that a randomly selected student takes Spanish is 0.45, the probability the student takes music is 0.30, and the probability the student takes both is 0.10. What is the probability that a randomly selected student takes Spanish or music (or both)?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.65

stem: For two events A and B, P(A) = 0.70, P(B) = 0.40, and P(A and B) = 0.35. What is P(A or B)?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.75

stem: Among 80 students surveyed, 50 own a laptop, 30 own a tablet, and 15 own both. What is the probability that a randomly selected student from this group owns a laptop or a tablet?

A new thermometer is tested thousands of times on liquids with known temperatures. Its readings are tightly clustered, but they average 2.3 degrees above the true temperature no matter how many readings are averaged. What is the main problem?
criteria: A. The estimator has high variability, since its readings are not equal to the true temperature.
B. The readings are not independent, since each is above the true temperature.
C. The sample sizes are too small, since averaging more readings would remove the error.
D. (correct) The estimator is biased, since its readings are centered above the true value.

stem: In repeated random samples of size 100 from a population with true mean 50, a new estimator has a sampling distribution centered at 56 with a standard deviation of 1.5. Which statement best describes this estimator?
criteria: A. It is unbiased with low variability, because its standard deviation is small.
B. It is biased with high variability, since its values are far from 50.
C. It is unbiased but has high variability, since it often misses 50.
D. (correct) It is biased but has low variability: its values cluster near 56 instead of 50.

stem: A statistician simulates 2,000 random samples to estimate a true proportion of 0.40. The 2,000 sample proportions average exactly 0.40, but individual values range from 0.25 to 0.55. Which statement is correct?
criteria: A. (correct) The estimator is unbiased but has high variability: its average is 0.40, yet single estimates are widely spread.
B. The estimator is unbiased, so increasing the sample size cannot reduce how widely the estimates vary.
C. The estimator is biased, because many individual estimates differ from the true proportion of 0.40.
D. The estimator is unbiased with low variability, because its average equals 0.40.

stem: In a random sample of 250 adults, 105 say they use public transit weekly. A researcher wants to know whether the proportion of all adults who use public transit weekly is less than 0.45. Which hypotheses should be tested?
criteria: A. (correct) H₀: p = 0.45, Hₐ: p < 0.45

stem: A manufacturer says 10% of its chips are defective. In a random sample of 300 chips, 45 are defective. A quality inspector wants to know whether the true defect rate differs from 10%. Which hypotheses are correct?
criteria: C. (correct) H₀: p = 0.10, Hₐ: p ≠ 0.10

stem: A candidate needs more than 40% of voters to win. In a random sample of 80 voters, 38 support the candidate. The campaign wants to test whether the proportion of all voters supporting the candidate exceeds 40%. Which hypotheses are correct?
criteria: A. (correct) H₀: p = 0.40, Hₐ: p > 0.40

stem: A basketball player makes each free throw independently with probability 0.3. Let X be the number of free throws made in 4 attempts. What is P(X = 0)?
criteria: B. (correct) 0.2401

stem: Each seed in a packet of 6 sprouts independently with probability 0.2. Let X be the number of seeds that sprout. What is P(X = 0)?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.2621

stem: A pollster makes 8 independent phone calls. Each call is answered with probability 0.35. Let X be the number of calls that are answered. What is P(X = 0)?
criteria: A. (correct) 0.0319

stem: Two researchers test the same hypotheses and the same true parameter value. Study X uses α = 0.10 with n = 400. Study Y uses α = 0.01 with n = 100. Which statement about their power is correct?
criteria: A. The studies have equal power, because they test the same hypotheses with the same true parameter value.
B. (correct) Study Y has lower power, because both its smaller α and smaller sample size reduce power.
C. Study X has lower power, because the larger α makes a Type I error more likely, which reduces power.
D. Study X has lower power, because a larger sample size increases variability and so makes rejection less likely.

stem: A test of H₀: p = 0.50 versus Hₐ: p > 0.50 uses n = 100 and α = 0.05, and the true proportion is p = 0.60. Which change would increase the power of the test?
criteria: A. (correct) Increasing the sample size to 400, which reduces the standard error.
B. Decreasing the sample size to 25, since a smaller sample has fewer chances for error.
C. Lowering α to 0.01, which makes the test more careful about rejecting.
D. Using the hypothesized value 0.58 in place of 0.50, so the null is closer to the truth.

stem: A significance test with α = 0.05 has a Type II error probability of 0.35 when the true proportion is 0.60. What is the power of the test against that alternative?
criteria: D. (correct) 0.65

stem: A medical team tests whether a new drug lowers systolic blood pressure more than a placebo. They enroll 36 patients, 18 men and 18 women, and randomly assign drug or placebo separately within the men and within the women, instead of randomizing all 36 patients together. What is the main statistical advantage of assigning treatments within each sex?
criteria: A. It lets the team conclude the drug works for all adults, since both sexes were included in the trial.
B. It makes the placebo group unnecessary, because sex differences are already accounted for.
C. It eliminates confounding from every lurking variable, including ones the team never measured.
D. (correct) It removes blood-pressure variation that is due to sex from the drug-versus-placebo comparison, making a real drug effect easier to detect.

stem: A teacher wants to compare a new study app with textbook review. She has 60 students: 30 in a morning section and 30 in an afternoon section. Within each section she randomly assigns half the students to the app and half to the textbook, rather than randomizing all 60 together. What is the primary benefit of this approach?
criteria: A. It allows the teacher to claim cause and effect, which complete randomization of all 60 students would not allow.
B. It guarantees the class period has no effect on test scores in either treatment group.
C. It makes the app and textbook groups larger, which gives more data for the comparison.
D. (correct) It accounts for score differences caused by class period, so differences between the two study methods stand out more clearly.

stem: A veterinary researcher compares two diets for weight loss in 24 dogs: 12 small-breed dogs and 12 large-breed dogs. Diet is randomly assigned separately within the small-breed group and within the large-breed group. Compared with randomly assigning diets to all 24 dogs at once, what does this design mainly accomplish?
criteria: A. It makes the dogs and owners unaware of which diet each dog receives, so expectations cannot affect results.
B. It raises the number of dogs in the study from 24 to 48, which strengthens the evidence.
C. It removes the need for a second diet group because breed size is already being compared.
D. (correct) It controls variation in weight loss that is related to breed size, so a real difference between the diets is easier to detect.

stem: A random sample of 600 teenagers in a school district is used to build a 90% confidence interval for the proportion of all teenagers in the district who own a laptop. The interval is (0.28, 0.36). Which statement is a correct interpretation?
criteria: A. 90% of teenagers in the district own a laptop, give or take 4 percentage points.
B. There is a 90% probability that a new random sample of 600 teenagers will have a sample proportion between 0.28 and 0.36.
C. Between 28% and 36% of the 600 sampled teenagers own a laptop, and we are 90% sure of this.
D. (correct) We are 90% confident that the interval from 0.28 to 0.36 captures the proportion of all teenagers in the district who own a laptop.

stem: A news site reports a 95% confidence interval of (0.52, 0.60) for the proportion of registered voters in a county who favor a school bond, using a random sample of 1,000 voters. Which statement correctly explains what the 95% confidence level means?
criteria: A. About 95% of the 1,000 voters in the sample favor the school bond, give or take a few points.
B. (correct) About 95% of intervals built this way from repeated random samples would contain the true proportion.
C. There is a 5% chance that this sample proportion lies outside the interval from 0.52 to 0.60.
D. The probability is 0.95 that the true proportion of supporters in the county is exactly 0.56.

stem: A company surveys a random sample of 1,200 of its customers and computes a 99% confidence interval of (0.71, 0.79) for the proportion of all its customers who are satisfied. Which statement is a correct interpretation of this interval?
criteria: A. About 99% of the 1,200 surveyed customers gave a satisfaction rating between 0.71 and 0.79.
B. (correct) We are 99% confident that the true proportion of all the company's customers who are satisfied is between 0.71 and 0.79.
C. There is a 99% probability that the next customer surveyed will be satisfied.
D. The true proportion of satisfied customers changes from sample to sample and falls between 0.71 and 0.79 in 99% of samples.

stem: A pediatrician tells a parent that a baby's weight is at the 20th percentile for babies of the same age. What does this mean?
criteria: A. This baby weighs 20% less than the average baby of the same age.
B. About 20% of babies that age weigh more than this baby.
C. (correct) About 20% of babies that age weigh the same as or less than this baby.
D. This baby's weight is 20% of the way from the lightest to the heaviest baby.

stem: A class of 40 students takes a quiz. Exactly 32 of the 40 scores, including Dana's, are less than or equal to Dana's score. Which percentile is Dana's score?
criteria: A. (correct) 80th percentile
B. 20th percentile
C. 8th percentile
D. 32nd percentile

stem: An employee at a large company learns that her salary is at the 60th percentile of all salaries at the company. Which statement is correct?
criteria: A. (correct) About 60% of employees at the company earn her salary or less.
B. About 60% of employees at the company earn more than she does.
C. Her salary is 60% of the highest salary at the company.
D. She has the 60th highest salary among the employees at the company.

stem: Researchers examine the medical records of 500 adults, noting whether each person takes a daily vitamin D supplement and whether the person had a bone fracture in the past five years. The researchers do not tell anyone to start or stop taking supplements. What type of study is this?
criteria: A. A single-blind experiment
B. (correct) An observational study
C. A randomized block experiment
D. A completely randomized experiment

stem: A teacher lets her 40 students choose either flashcards or practice tests as their study method for a unit, then compares the two groups' scores on the unit exam. What type of study is this?
criteria: A. A randomized block design, because the students form two groups.
B. A randomized experiment, because the teacher compared two study methods.
C. (correct) An observational study, because students chose their own study method instead of being assigned one.
D. A matched-pairs experiment, because every student took the same exam.

stem: Researchers randomly assign 90 volunteers to one of three diets and measure each volunteer's cholesterol level after eight weeks. What type of study is this?
criteria: A. An observational study, because cholesterol was only measured at the end.
B. (correct) A randomized experiment, because the researchers assigned the diets to the volunteers at random.
C. An observational study, because the volunteers were not a random sample of adults.
D. A sample survey, because 90 people provided data.

stem: A school district wants to learn parents' opinions about school lunches. It mails questionnaires only to the families listed in the PTA directory. Which bias is most likely?
criteria: A. Voluntary response bias, because parents decide whether to fill out the form.
B. (correct) Undercoverage bias, because parents not in the PTA directory have no chance to be selected.
C. Nonresponse bias, because some mailed questionnaires will not be returned.
D. No bias, because every questionnaire was sent by the same method.

stem: A radio station asks listeners to call in during a morning show to vote on whether the city should build a new stadium, and it reports the percent of callers in favor. What is the most likely source of bias?
criteria: A. No bias, because a large number of listeners will call in.
B. (correct) Voluntary response bias, because only listeners with strong opinions are likely to call.
C. Placebo effect, because the callers believe their vote matters.
D. Confounding bias, because a lurking variable is mixed with the stadium vote.

stem: A city randomly selects 1,000 households from a complete list of all households and mails each a survey about recycling. Only 220 households return it. Which bias is most likely?
criteria: A. Undercoverage bias, because 780 households are missing from the data.
B. Response bias, because the survey asked about recycling.
C. (correct) Nonresponse bias, because households that did not reply may differ from those that did.
D. Convenience sampling bias, because mailed surveys are the cheapest approach.

stem: At a high school, a student is chosen at random. Let C be the event that the student is in a club and J the event that the student has a part-time job. P(C) = 0.50, P(J) = 0.20, and P(C and J) = 0.15. Are C and J independent?
criteria: A. No, because P(C and J) = 0.15 is not equal to P(C) + P(J) = 0.70.
B. Yes, because P(C or J) = 0.55 is less than 1.
C. (correct) No, because P(C)P(J) = 0.10, which does not equal P(C and J) = 0.15.
D. Yes, because P(C and J) = 0.15 is smaller than both P(C) and P(J).

stem: At a school, P(a student rides the bus) = 0.50 and P(a student wears glasses) = 0.20. Among students who ride the bus, 20% wear glasses. Are riding the bus and wearing glasses independent?
criteria: A. (correct) Yes, because P(glasses | bus) = 0.20 equals P(glasses) = 0.20.
B. No, because P(glasses | bus) = 0.20 is much smaller than P(bus) = 0.50.
C. Yes, because P(bus) + P(glasses) = 0.70, which is less than 1.
D. No, because both events can occur together, with P(bus and glasses) = 0.10 > 0.

stem: A cafe records 300 orders. Of these, 120 included coffee, 90 included a pastry, and 45 included both. For a randomly chosen order, are 'includes coffee' and 'includes a pastry' independent?
criteria: A. No, because 45 does not equal 120 + 90 = 210.
B. Yes, because 120 + 90 = 210, which is less than the 300 orders.
C. Yes, because the 45 orders with both are fewer than the 120 or the 90 orders with each item.
D. (correct) No, because P(coffee and pastry) = 45/300 = 0.15, which differs from P(coffee)P(pastry) = 0.40 x 0.30 = 0.12.

stem: A student is chosen at random from a high school. Event S is that the student is a senior and event F is that the student is a freshman. Are S and F mutually exclusive?
criteria: A. Yes, because being a senior and being a freshman are independent events.
B. No, because P(S) + P(F) is less than 1.
C. No, because both groups belong to the same school.
D. (correct) Yes, because a student cannot be both a senior and a freshman, so P(S and F) = 0.

stem: A student is chosen at random from a school. Event S is that the student plays on the soccer team and event O is that the student plays in the school orchestra. Are S and O mutually exclusive?
criteria: A. No, but only if S and O are independent.
B. Yes, because P(S and O) must equal P(S)P(O).
C. Yes, because soccer and orchestra are different activities.
D. (correct) No, because a student can play on the soccer team and also play in the orchestra.

stem: A bag holds marbles of several colors. One marble is drawn at random. The probability it is red is 0.30 and the probability it is blue is 0.45. What is the probability that the marble is red or blue?
criteria: D. (correct) 0.75

stem: Waiting times at a clinic have a strongly right-skewed distribution. A researcher takes many random samples of n = 64 patients and computes the sample mean wait time for each. Why is the sampling distribution of the sample mean approximately normal?
criteria: A. Because the individual wait times themselves become normally distributed once n = 64 is reached.
B. (correct) By the CLT, means of large random samples are approximately normal, even when the population is skewed.
C. Because the 64 patients sampled are less than 10% of all patients at the clinic.
D. Because the sample mean is an unbiased estimator of the population mean wait time.

stem: A population of household incomes is strongly right-skewed. A statistician draws many random samples of size n = 2 and many of size n = 100, and plots the sample means from each. Which statement is correct?
criteria: A. (correct) The means from n = 100 will look approximately normal, but the means from n = 2 will still be noticeably right-skewed.
B. The n = 2 means will look more normal than the n = 100 means, because small samples contain less skew.
C. Both sets of sample means will look approximately normal, because every mean is an average.
D. Neither set will look normal, because a skewed population cannot give a normal sampling distribution.

stem: A population of delivery times is heavily right-skewed with mean 45 minutes. Many random samples of n = 40 deliveries are taken and each sample mean is plotted in a dotplot. Which describes the dotplot and the reason?
criteria: A. Left-skewed, because averaging 40 times pulls the mean away from the long right tail.
B. (correct) Approximately normal in shape, because the Central Limit Theorem applies to means of samples this large.
C. Right-skewed like the population, because sample means keep the shape of the population.
D. Uniform between the smallest and largest delivery times, because each sample mean is equally likely.

stem: Suppose 30% of all students at a university commute by bike. A random sample of n = 200 students is selected. What is the standard deviation (standard error) of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion of bike commuters?
In a large city, 55% of residents support a new park. A random sample of n = 150 residents is taken. Find the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion in favor.
A factory knows that 12% of its widgets are defective. An inspector randomly selects n = 400 widgets. What is the standard error of the sample proportion of defective widgets?

Two researchers test the same hypotheses about a population proportion using the same sample size and the same true proportion. Researcher 1 uses a significance level of alpha = 0.10 and Researcher 2 uses alpha = 0.01. Which test has greater power?
criteria: A. Researcher 2's test, because a lower Type I error rate also means a lower Type II error rate.
B. (correct) Researcher 1's test, because a larger alpha makes rejecting the null hypothesis easier when it is false.
C. They have equal power, because both use the same hypotheses and sample size.
D. Researcher 2's test, because a smaller alpha requires stronger evidence.

stem: Two tests of H0: p = 0.50 vs Ha: p > 0.50 use the same sample size and significance level. In one situation the true proportion is 0.55, and in the other the true proportion is 0.70. Which situation gives the test greater power?
criteria: A. They have the same power, because the sample size and alpha are the same.
B. The situation with true p = 0.55, because it is closer to the null value.
C. (correct) The situation with true p = 0.70, because a larger gap from the null value makes a false null easier to detect.
D. The situation with true p = 0.55, because power equals the Type I error probability alpha.

stem: A school district tests H0: a new tutoring program does not change mean reading scores against Ha: the program raises mean reading scores. In this setting, what does the power of the test measure for a particular size of improvement?
criteria: A. The chance the test rejects H0 when the program has no effect on scores.
B. (correct) The chance the test rejects H0 when the program truly raises scores by that amount.
C. The chance that the program truly raises reading scores, given the data.
D. The chance the test fails to reject H0 when the program truly raises scores.

stem: A test of whether a new bus route changes the proportion of on-time arrivals gives p = 0.03 with alpha = 0.05. Which conclusion is correct?
criteria: A. (correct) Reject H0; there is convincing statistical evidence for the alternative hypothesis at the 0.05 level.
B. Reject H0, which proves the alternative hypothesis is true.
C. Fail to reject H0, because 0.03 is smaller than 0.05 and so the evidence is too weak.
D. Reject H0; the probability that H0 is true is 0.03.

stem: A researcher chooses alpha = 0.10 before testing whether a new fertilizer changes mean plant height and obtains p = 0.08. Which conclusion is correct?
criteria: A. Fail to reject H0, since p = 0.08 is greater than the usual cutoff of 0.05.
B. Reject H0, and the probability of a Type I error in this study is exactly 0.08.
C. Fail to reject H0, which shows H0 is true.
D. (correct) Reject H0, since p = 0.08 is less than the chosen significance level of 0.10.

stem: A hospital tests whether a new protocol reduces readmission rates and uses alpha = 0.01. The test gives p = 0.047. Which conclusion is correct?
criteria: A. Reject H0, since p = 0.047 is below the common 0.05 cutoff.
B. Fail to reject H0, which means H0 is true with probability 1 - 0.047 = 0.953.
C. (correct) Fail to reject H0; there is not convincing evidence at the 0.01 level.
D. Reject H0, since 0.047 is close to 0.01.
